summary: Policy ingest lag in support-orchestrator leading to escalation-owner flapping and delayed SLA calculations
description: Issue summary: After a policy publish window on 2026-03-01 ~09:10 UTC, the support-orchestrator ingestion path showed sustained lag (~10-25m) causing escalation_owner to flip between default on-call user and team-owned on escalate attempts. Impact: SLA calculations for routed tickets were delayed and the daily routing report showed gaps. Users reported incorrect owner assignment for a subset of internal tickets, leading to missed P1 handoffs. This ticket captures triage, investigation, fix, and follow-ups.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a new escalation policy via Policy UI that sets escalation_owner to a named team user.
2) Publish policy and observe the policy-engine change events emitted to the policy-topic.
3) Watch support-orchestrator consumer lag in the consumer group dashboard (kafka-consumer-offsets).
4) Trigger a test ticket that should pick up the new owner (simulate via support API).
Expected: owner is applied within 30s and SLA calc runs. Observed: owner either remains default or flips during retries and SLA calc delayed by up to 25m.
logs:
[2026-03-01T09:12:03Z] support-orchestrator[consumer]: WARN consumer lag: 13489 msgs behind
[2026-03-01T09:12:06Z] support-orchestrator[ingest]: ERROR failed to apply policy change: null value for escalation_owner at policy_id=pol-2048
[2026-03-01T09:12:07Z] support-orchestrator[ingest]: INFO scheduling retry backoff=30s attempt=1
[2026-03-01T09:23:12Z] support-orchestrator[metrics]: WARN sla-calc-delay=1200s tickets_pending=42
(see attached support-orchestrator.log excerpt in attachments)
investigation_notes: Timeline: 09:10 publish -> 09:12 consumer lag spikes -> 09:15 first ERRORs for null escalation_owner -> 09:40 backlog processed intermittently -> 10:00 most policies reconciled. Hypothesis 1: recent policy-engine v2.3.7 allowed nullable escalation_owner on intermediate schema causing parser to emit nulls. Hypothesis 2: consumer backpressure + large GC pause in support-orchestrator pod slowed reprocessing and exponential backoff amplified delay. Verified: support-orchestrator pods showed a 2.3s stop-the-world GC at 09:11 with 40% CPU saturation; policy-engine PR 1123 introduced a change to policy schema (owner can be omitted) without downstream defensive handling. Repro: Applied a crafted policy missing owner field in staging and observed same null parse path and owner fallback behavior. Metrics: policy-ingest error rate peaked at 7.8% and sla-calc latency 20x baseline during the window.
comments: Support (Tanya): Customer-facing symptom reported by internal ops at 09:25 UTC; escalated to SRE.
SRE (Luca): Identified consumer lag and GC spike in support-orchestrator. Pinning pods and pulling logs for span. Noted recent deployment of policy-engine v2.3.7 in prod at 08:58 UTC.
Eng (Mateo): Timesketch of PR 1123 shows optional owner field. Suggest immediate rollback and hotfix to handle null owners gracefully.
Support (Asha): Created this ticket and added nightly routing report snapshot for affected hours. Requested backfill of SLA metrics once fix is deployed.
SRE (Luca): Rolled back support-orchestrator to prior JVM tuning and cleared consumer group offsets for a controlled replay. Monitoring backlog drain now at 2026-03-04 02:14 UTC.
Eng (Mateo): Deployed hotfix v2.3.8 to policy-engine to enforce owner defaulting and validation at publish time. Patch set: PR 1129.
Support (Tanya): Verified owner assignment on sampled tickets; routing report reprocessed and reconciled. Marking as resolved pending follow-ups.
resolution_notes: Short-term remediation: rolled back problematic consumer JVM flags, cleared and rebalanced consumer offsets, and applied hotfix to policy-engine (v2.3.8) that restores non-null escalation_owner default and rejects malformed policy publishes. Long-term: added a defensive parse layer in support-orchestrator to ignore null owner and emit a clear validation metric. Backfill: reprocessed the policy change stream for the impacted window and re-ran SLA calc job for tickets created between 2026-03-01T09:00 and 2026-03-01T11:00; results ingested into daily routing report.
root_cause: Regression introduced in policy-engine v2.3.7 that made escalation_owner optional at publish time, combined with lack of defensive parsing in support-orchestrator and a concurrent JVM GC/CPU pressure that amplified consumer lag and retry backoff leading to owner flapping and delayed SLA calculations.
follow_up_actions:
1) Add unit and integration tests that publish policies with missing owner to prevent regressions (owner required at policy publish).
2) Add a validation gate in the Policy UI that prevents publish when owner is missing for escalation policies.
3) Create a support-orchestrator health dashboard: consumer lag, owner-null-rate, sla-calc-latency.
4) Update runbook (confluence) with step-by-step for clearing consumer backlogs and safe replay.
5) Release post-mortem summary to #support and ops channels.
6) Schedule a changelog review for 2.3.x releases to catch schema drift with consumers.
